articles.title: Louzán confirma la noticia de MARCA: Mestalla tendrá su adiós a la Selección en la Nations League
articles.standfirst: El Presidente de la Federación confirma que el estadio valencianista acogerá los cuartos de final de la competición europea
articles.summary: Contactos con la Federación para último baile de la selección en el templo valencianista
articles.body: El Valencia quiere que Mestalla tenga su último baile con la Selección. Hace ya tiempo que desde el club se contactó con la Federación para que España juegue en la casa del Valencia antes de eche el cierre al acabar la Liga. La repuesta fue afirmativa, para jugar en junio. Eso era incluír a Valencia en la candidatura española para la Final Four de la Nations. Madrid y Mestalla eran la idea primigenia. Pero desde el Valencia se comunicó que esa idea era un riesgo porque el último partido en casa puede dejar el estadio en condiciones poco recomendables. La noticia adelantada por MARCA fue confirmada por Louzán. El presidente de la Federación española de Fútbol estuvo presente en el homenaje a Luis de la Fuente en el barrio de Monteolivete en el que se muestra el mural del seleccionador siendo manteado por los jugadores tras la final del mundial. "En este Mestalla mítico será el último partido de la selección aquí. Estamos todos con esa iniciativa y el ayuntamiento de Valencia también está a nuestro lado. Será un partido muy bonito ojalá sea el de vuelta y podamos contar5 más triunfos para la selección española". Nou Mestalla, sede en el Mundial: "Estamos trabajando con los técnicos de FIFA porque hemos pedido que vengan a Valencia antes de final de año para lo que puede ser y yo espero que sea sede del Mundial 2030. La final: "Estamos trabajando para ellos y no ofrecen dudas. España tiene las garantías de éxito para que la final se juegue en España y debemos seguir trabajando en esa línea" El Valencia quiere que ese partido sea en marzo, en los cuartos de final de la Nations League, ronda para la que España ya está clasificada. Desde Las Rozas se tomó nota, aunque es una decisión pendiente de tomar. La RFEF tiene compromisos pendientes, como jugar en Las Palmas, aunque este caso encaja más con la clasificación para para la Euro 2028. Mestalla es un campo con una vinculación muy especial con la selección. Fue su casa en el Mundial de 1982 y allí se han vivido partidos memorables, como el 9-0 a Austria con Camacho. La última aparición de España en el estadio del murciélago fue en los cuartos de final de la pasada Nations. Tras empatar a dos con Holanda en Rotterdam, la vuelta fue un 3-3 reuelto a favor del equipo de Luis de la Fuente en los penalits.

articles.title: Alabama's Ryan Coleman-Williams Says He's 'Literally Like Spider-Man' After Fixing Drop Issues
articles.summary: Alabama wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams thinks he compares favorably to a beloved superhero after working to fix the drop issues that plagued his 2025 season.
articles.body:
Alabama wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams thinks he compares favorably to a beloved superhero after working to fix the drop issues that plagued his 2025 season.

Speaking to ESPN's Alex Scarborough , Coleman-Williams described himself as being "literally like Spider-Man" amid his streak of four consecutive games without a drop.

"Now, when it comes to the ball, I'm literally like Spider-Man. It's a lot easier," he said. "It's night and day."

Never-Before-Seen Vid of Saban Benching Hurts 🎥

Coleman-Williams has had a roller-coaster ride throughout his college career thus far. He arrived at Alabama in 2024 as arguably the best freshman wide receiver recruit in the country, a class that also included Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith.

After a strong debut season with 865 yards and eight touchdowns, Coleman-Williams took a step back in 2025. He put up 689 yards and four touchdowns, but most concerning was a 16.9 percent drop rate.

It looked like that was going to carry over into 2026 when Coleman-Williams had two drops through the first two quarters of Alabama's season-opening win over East Carolina.

To help fix the issue, Alabama head athletic trainer Jeff Allen told Scarborough they used virtual reality training during the offseason.

The results are showing up on the stat sheet. Coleman-Williams doesn't have a drop in his last four games, has already matched his touchdown total from 2025 and is averaging a career-high 18.8 yards per reception.

Alabama will need Coleman-Williams to show off his Spider-Man hands on Saturday when it hosts No. 2 Georgia in a game that could determine one of the two representatives in the SEC Championship Game.

articles.title: Gabriel Jesus, la primera apuesta goleadora de Flick ante la baja de Raphinha
articles.standfirst: Será titular contra el Getafe: el ex del Leeds tampoco estará frente al Galatasaray
articles.summary: Será titular contra el Getafe: el ex del Leeds tampoco estará frente al Galatasaray
articles.body: El Barça está atemorizado, por no decir aterrorizado, ante la idea de perder por una recaída a Raphinha, de ahí que el brasileño no vaya a participar en los dos próximos encuentros del bloque azulgrana. El atacante regresó de la cita con Brasil antes de tiempo a causa de un edema en la parte posterior del muslo derecho. No es una dolencia grave, pero realiza trabajo individualizado y descansará unos días. Todos imponen la máxima cautela y precaución. Flick tiene, además, alternativas al ex del Leeds en el vestuario. "En las pruebas de imagen a las que se sometió Raphinha no se vio que sufriera una lesión importante, pero hay que reaccionar y hay que preocuparse por él porque el año pasado sufrió tres lesiones. Le cuidaremos. No estará mañana ni tampoco en la cita de Estambul contra el Galatasaray", comentó Hansi Flick este viernes. Más claro no pudo ser el preparador culé. El internacional brasileño se lesionó durante el segundo partido de Brasil contra Australia y regresó antes de tiempo a Barcelona. Nadie quiere correr riesgos con él. De ahí que avanzara su vuelta y de que vaya a descansar en los dos próximos encuentros. En su caso, llueve sobre mojado: el curso pasado se perdió ¡26! encuentros a causa de distintas dolencias en la misma zona que ahora: el muslo. Flick le dosifica por miedo a una recaída a pesar de que es su futbolista más determinante: es el Pichichi del equipo con 14 goles y de LaLiga, con 12. Pero es más grande el temor a perderlo durante más tiempo. Además, el preparador culé tiene alternativas para la posición de 9. Aunque para el cruce contra el Getafe ya está decidido y definido quién jugará: Gabriel Jesus. Lo avanzó el técnico germano. "La idea es que sea titular, ha mejorado mucho. Se ha adaptado muy bien. Su punto fuerte está dentro del área. Se ha entrenado bien. Me gusta lo que veo de Gabriel Jesus", comentó Flick en la previa contra el Getafe. El brasileño, firmado este verano, suma sólo 41 minutos repartidos en cuatro partidos, pero le han bastado para marcar dos goles. Resulta realmente efectivo. El preparador también tiene, no obstante, otras variantes, para la delantera, como colocar al joven Hamza Abdelkarim, Olmo, Adeyemi, Gordon e incluso Lamine Yamal. De hecho, no se descarta que alguno de ellos juegue el próximo martes contra el Galatasaray en la punta del ataque culé. De momento, lo único claro es que Gabriel Jesus suplirá a Raphinha contra el Getafe. No se sabe si el ex del Arsenal se mantendrá en el once en la Champions League. Frente al Betis, a priori, ya está recuperado el Pichichi azulgrana.

articles.title: Shai y la conexión canadiense: Atlético Ottawa y Jonathan David
articles.standfirst: La llegada del nuevo inversor amplía el vínculo con el país norteamericano
articles.summary: La llegada del nuevo inversor amplía el vínculo con el país norteamericano
articles.body: Primero, Jonathan David, presentado el 1 de septiembre como el primer canadiense de la historia del Atlético. Un hito que está siendo respondido con goles. Los que convierten al jugador cedido por la Juventus en el sexto rojiblanco de la historia que marca en sus tres primeros partidos en LaLiga. Este 8 de octubre, en exclusiva de MARCA, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander se ha convertido en nuevo inversor rojiblanco. El doble MVP de la NBA (que hace unos meses apareció con un chándal de los rojiblancos) vuelve a colocar al país norteamericano en el mapa rojiblanco. Lo hace siendo una súper estrella del deporte en un país, Estados Unidos, que el Atlético se ha propuesto cono objetivo para seguir su expansión internacional. Antes de ambos, claro, el Atlético compró el Atlético Ottawa siguiendo a otras franquicias como la mexicana de San Luis. Un vínculo que se mantiene y que eleva este tridente peculiar con un país que hasta hace nada no tenía recorrido en clave rojiblanca, pero que ahora cuenta con dos de sus deportistas más mediáticos. El de Shai no es, en cualquier caso, el único deportista de élite que invierte en equipos de fútbol. Así, Kevin Durant asesora al PSG en su estrategia multideporte y en ayudar a su desarrollo en EE.UU. Otra leyenda, Tom Brady, preside un consejo asesor en el Birmingham City.

articles.title: Luis de la Fuente: "Siempre cuidamos a los jugadores y es bueno que técnicos como Flick lo valoren"
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador nacional acude a un homenaje en Valencia ante el mural en el que le mantean los jugadores de la selección
articles.summary: El seleccionador nacional acude a un homenaje en Valencia ante el mural en el que le mantean los jugadores de la selección
articles.body: El seleccionador nacional, Luis de la Fuente, ha visitado este viernes, 9 d’Octubre, el mural dedicado a la selección española de fútbol que el Ayuntamiento de València ha instalado en el barrio de Montolivete. La obra, realizada por el artista Alberto León, ocupa la fachada del Centro Municipal de Actividades para Personas Mayores de Montolivete, en la plaza Vicente Alcober Coloma. El mural representa una de las imágenes de la celebración del campeonato: Luis de la Fuente levantando la Copa del Mundo mientras los jugadores de la selección lo mantean. "Estoy abrumado y emocionado. Es algo que se escapa de lo que uno se puede imaginar con tanto cariño. Es un homenaje a un grupo de futbolistas excepcionales y a un país entregado con su selección. Yo debuté en Mestalla en primera división, sería maravilloso jugar con España ya estuvimos hace poco con un ambiente excepcional. Mestalla es un campo histórico y mítico. La experiencia de estar aquí fue buenísima y reunimos casi 30.000 personas en el entrenamiento. Nosotros trabajamos siempre para cuidar a los jugadores y priorizamos cuida a los jugadores. Nos gusta que los entrenadores como Flick lo sepan y lo valoren", comentó el seleccionador a las preguntas de los periodistas presentes en el acto. Vandalizado en Barcelona La pieza tiene además una historia particular. Alberto León recuperó en València una obra que había realizado anteriormente en Barcelona y que fue vandalizada poco después de su creación. A petición de la Junta Municipal de Russafa, el artista recreó el mural en una superficie de mayores dimensiones e incorporó mejoras técnicas destinadas a facilitar su conservación y protegerlo frente al vandalismo. Previamente a la visita al mural en cuestión, el seleccionador, acompañado por Louzán, presidente de la RFEF y por Gomar, presidente de la FFCV, estuvo en la recepción oficial con el presidente de la Generalitat Valenciana Juan Francisco Pérez Llorca en el Palau tras la entrega de los galardones del Nou D'Octubre.

articles.title: Everton up for sale: What next as owners TFG look for a way out?
articles.summary: Everton are up for sale again. Chief football writer Phil McNulty looks at what happens next as owners The Friedkin Group look for a way out.
articles.body:
When Everton 's owners The Friedkin Group released a 170-word statement on Friday morning announcing they were effectively putting the club up for sale, it was as low-key and underwhelming as their tenure on Merseyside.

TFG, also owners of AS Roma in Italy's Serie A, paid more than £400m for a 99.5% share of Everton in December 2024, releasing the club from the financial crisis and toxicity that characterised the final days of Farhad Moshiri's chaotic regime.

It was meant to be the start of a bold new era for the club as they waited to move out of Goodison Park into a magnificent new stadium at Bramley Moore Dock.

Instead, TFG will now test the market, with football finance expert Kieran Maguire telling BBC Sport he expected them to seek a price between £750m and £800m for a complete sale, taking on current debts of around £468m.

In contrast to the high hopes and confidence that accompanied their arrival, TFG have effectively been absentee owners focusing their efforts on Roma - a stance illustrated by the fact chairman Dan Friedkin has never attended an Everton game or, even more startlingly, never spoken to manager David Moyes since he arrived back at the club in January 2025.

Moyes made that revelation in the aftermath of a botched summer transfer window that transformed the relationship between Everton 's fans and TFG from cold acceptance to outright toxicity.

Everton owners consider selling club two years after takeover

Everton told to pay Burnley £35m over PSR breach

The catalyst was TFG's attempt to sell teenager Harrison Armstrong, one of the finest products of Everton 's Academy in recent years, to Nottingham Forest in a £40m deal.

The move was agreed by TFG until news leaked out, prompting loud threats of "a riot" from Everton fans during the game at Bournemouth later that day.

Such was the reaction, TFG went into damage limitation mode to block the deal for the 19-year-old midfielder, but it was little more than a face-saving PR exercise after a catastrophic decision that instantly alienated the fanbase.

Everton then sold Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City for £65m and striker Beto - hardly elite but a recognised striker - to Fiorentina, before a move for Monaco forward Folarin Balogun collapsed with no time to seek alternatives.

It left Moyes a striker light and with only 18 senior outfield players. From that moment the credits were rolling for TFG, leading to the announcement they are looking to sell their stake in the club.

Why have TFG decided now is the time to sell?

Maguire said: "I think there are various factors at play. I suspect they were shocked by having to pay Burnley more than £35m for a breach of financial rules."

In 2024 Everton were found to have broken Profit and Sustainability Rules (PSR) over a three-year period. Burnley argued the breach had impacted their chances of staying in the Premier League in the 2021-22 season and sought compensation for the losses associated with being relegated.

TFG injected £38m into the club to cover the cost, while Everton have subsequently appealed.

"I think that perhaps they thought English football was going to become as litigious as trying to operate in the United States," added Maguire. "This will not have appealed to them.

"It is also a good time to sell because it is such a buoyant market. The Americans will be interested. There are only 20 Premier League clubs you can buy. There are lots of potential buyers out there. There is that scarcity factor.

"I'd say TFG will look for £750m to £800m to sell. It can take 5 billion dollars or even more to buy a sporting franchise in the United States.

"I think they can see this as something they can flip - in other words, buy low and sell high."

What TFG have brought to Everton is a measure of financial stability following Moshiri's era of crisis, which Maguire believes will make them an attractive proposition to potential suitors.

" Everton have history and heritage," he said. They are Premier League perennials. They look like they will stay there and they have a passionate fanbase who fill a superb 50,000-plus stadium.

"You are not having to spend money on an upgrade of that stadium. I have a lot of respect for the finance people at the club. Unlike some of the chaos of Moshiri and what he left behind, you can lift up the carpet now at Everton and nothing unpleasant will come out.

"To paraphrase a former Prime Minister, you have got an 'over ready' football club coming on to the market. If you are an owner who wants to accelerate things at a football club, you have a starting point for that.

"And my start point for potential buyers would be the States."

There is no doubt, however, that Houston-based TFG's relationship with those back at base on Merseyside hinted at the dysfunctional.

The lack of a close relationship with manager Moyes was again emphasised when he admitted he only heard about Everton 's potential sale at the same time as the wider public - only adding to the sense of disconnect between TFG and the club, compared to how they work at Roma.

Speaking at his press conference before Sunday's match away at Hull, Moyes said: "I'm disappointed that Evertonians have to go through another period of 'who are our owners?'

"I truly believed with new ownership we were in it completely. My ambition coming back was trying to get Everton back to the levels they have been in the past, and that is challenging for Europe more often.

"It has been a difficult summer for us. I only found out this morning. Maybe, I am a little bit surprised, but maybe I shouldn't be that surprised."

On TFG's approach, Maguire added: "They have not really engaged with the club or Liverpool as a city. Dan Friedkin has never been to an Everton game, which shows the difference.

"With Roma, they have got a club in the Champions League - with all that entails financially - and one with a far greater chance of being there on a regular basis which, and we are only stating a fact, is not the case with Everton ."

"With a mixture of disappointment and indifference," added Maguire. "I think they now have the right people at Everton , while I think under the Moshiri regime there were some there for decoration rather than substance."

"Because so much due diligence has been done by the Friedkins themselves, all of the gremlins will have been highlighted and dealt with," said Maguire.

"It is now down to satisfying the Premier League's owners and directors' scenario. Are you a wrong 'un? Do you have the money? Can you prove where the money has come from - not just to buy the club but to run it?"

And Moyes is happy to give a reference as he added: "I'm looking forward to getting the right people in to take the club further forward.

"It's a great club. If anyone wants to speak to me then I will be the first person to let them know that it is certainly worth buying."

articles.summary: Jorge Salinas, Pablo García y Yassir Zabiri acudieron con sus respectivas selecciones
articles.body: El Racing ha tenido tres futbolistas que han ido con sus respectivas selecciones en este parón liguero. Jorge Salinas tan solo disputó un encuentro con la selección sub 20 española por lo que su ausencia fue mínima. Pero Pablo García y Zabiri han estado con sus países prácticamente lo que ha durado el parón. El internacional marroquí disputó pocos minutos con su país, mientras que Pablo García jugó los dos partidos completos con la sub 21. Sobre el extremos sevillano el técnico asturiano estaba feliz por su rendimiento, “Pablo García puede jugar de extremo, de segundo punta o de punta, es un goleador y todo lo que haga cerca del área rival tiene mucha posibilidad de éxito. Con España ha jugado como extremo derecho y ahí ha hecho muchos goles”. El Racing realizará este sábado la último sesión de trabajo previa al choque ante el Valencia y valorará la titularidad de Zabiri y Pablo García. Andrés Martín ya está a disposición de José Alberto y podrá disputar minutos ante el conjunto che.

articles.summary: El delantero, que había acusado una gripe a la vuelta de Guinea-Bisáu, reemplaza al central
articles.body: El Athletic ha comunicado una baja de última hora en la convocatoria para el partido de este sábado ante el Rayo. articles.title: Los campeones de la Intercontinental serán homenajeados en el Bernabéu
articles.standfirst: El equipo sub 20 dirigido por Álvaro López ofrecerá el histórico título juvenil conquistado el pasado 19 de septiembre
articles.summary: El equipo sub 20 de Álvaro López ofrecerá el título conquistado el pasado 19 de septiembre
articles.body: Después de 22 días, los campeones de la Intercontinental sub 20 vivirán otro momento inolvidable en el Bernabéu. Está todo preparado para que los 23 chicos de Álvaro López que se coronaron reyes del mundo el pasado 19 de septiembre ofrezcan a la afición el histórico título conquistado, el único que faltaba en las vitrinas de La Fábrica. El Madrid recibe al Villarreal este sábado a las 21.00 horas y poco antes del pitido inicial, el Bernabéu tendrá la oportunidad de rendir homenaje a sus jóvenes campeones. Un Bernabéu con más de 52.000 personas ya tuvo la oportunidad de disfrutar del triunfo en su momento y otro Bernabéu más lleno aún tendrá la ocasión de homenajearles y brindarles una cariñosa ovación. Javi Navarro, Illia, Álvaro González, Fortea, Bailón, Joan Martínez, Ariel, Mario Rivas, Aguado, Lezcano, Liberto, Cestero, Lacosta, Roberto Martín, Sergio Martínez, Beto, Carlos Díez, Adri Pérez, Yáñez, Ciria, Gabri Valero, Yeremaiah y Santamaría fueron los 23 jugadores que formaron la plantilla sub 20 del Real Madrid que afrontó la finalísima ante el Santiago Wanderers. Partido que acabó con 3-1 para los blancos, con goles de Yáñez, Santamaría y Roberto Martín. Un título con el que el técnico, Álvaro López, cerraba un círculo histórico conquistando con el Juvenil A Liga, Youth, Copa de Campeones e Intercontinental sub 20. Este sábado llegará el momento de un homenaje más que merecido. El Madrid ha podido cuadrar la agenda de todos los campeones, que juegan repartidos entre los tres primeros filiales. El Castilla juega este viernes, el Juvenil A lo hace el sábado a las 17.00 horas en Valdebebas y el Madrid C, el domingo a las 12.00 horas, también en Valdebebas.

articles.title: Hacker whose website triggered Manchester City probe to remain under police protection
articles.summary: Computer hacker Rui Pinto, who created the Football Leaks website that helped trigger the Premier League investigation into Manchester City's finances,
articles.body: Computer hacker Rui Pinto, who created the Football Leaks website that helped trigger the Premier League investigation into Manchester City's finances, will continue to receive police protection, Portuguese authorities confirmed on Friday.The protection measures were due to expire on Saturday but will remain in place until a new decision is made, Portugal's Justice Ministry said in a statement, news agency AFP reported.The ministry added that an earlier decision to end the protection had been cancelled because Pinto had not been "duly informed of the reasons for the decision" and had not been given an opportunity to challenge it.Pinto's lawyers had raised concerns last week over irregularities in the proceedings and the threats facing their client. The 37-year-old was assaulted in Lisbon last April and said he had to move to a secret location "due to the multiple death threats" he had received.Pinto has been a protected witness since 2020, when he agreed to give Portuguese authorities access to millions of files he had collected before his arrest.He was arrested in Hungary, where he was living, in January 2019 and extradited to Portugal. He spent more than a year in pre-trial detention before agreeing to cooperate with authorities by providing access to the encrypted data in his possession.Pinto has occupied two roles in the Portuguese justice system, as both a defendant and a protected witness. He is also cooperating with investigators in other European countries.During his first trial, the former history student and self-taught computer expert admitted hacking into computers to obtain millions of documents. He began publishing the material online in late 2015.The documents were later shared with a group of European investigative media organisations. articles.title: Gianni Infantino: Will anyone stop re-election of Fifa president?
articles.summary: Little more than two months since news broke of Infantino's Fifa Forward Enterprise proposal, the chances appear slim that Gianni Infantino might be removed as president.
articles.body:
Remember when pretty much everyone thought Gianni Infantino's days were numbered as Fifa president?

It is little more than two months since news broke of Infantino's Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, the plan to sell off commercial rights in the World Cup to a private equity firm.

Infantino, who had seemed impregnable as the head of world football's governing body, suddenly appeared not only to be vulnerable, but in fact in an untenable position.

Yet, with 40 days to go until the 18 November deadline for nominations for the presidential election, senior figures in world football now firmly believe the 56-year-old may well be unopposed.

Uefa thought that FFE had given it the chance to cut the head off the snake.

Except Uefa did not quite have the necessary weapons to pull it off, to overthrow a figure who has built up considerable levels of support in the rest of the world.

No election, no challenge, just another coronation at the Fifa Congress in Rabat on 18 March.

Right now, you cannot shake the feeling that Infantino has won.

Uefa fails to find anyone to stand against Infantino

Since summoning the Fifa management board to Rabat on 5 August to discuss FFE, Infantino has been on a tour of the world to cement his position.

To Colombia for the inauguration of the country's new president, Abelardo de la Espriella. Then visiting a Fifa-funded youth football tournament in the Dominican Republic.

At the weekend, he was at the Fifa Asean Cup final in Jakarta, Indonesia. And this week, an African football conference in Cape Verde.

It has been business as usual for the Swiss-Italian.

But there remains a rudimentary split in world football. Uefa, Concacaf and Asia against Infantino; Africa, South America and Oceania in support.

It raises the prospect that Infantino will be returned despite only carrying the backing of roughly half of Fifa's 211 members.

It is the funding model which has made Infantino's position so impenetrable, even in the face of accusations that he had worked against the wider interests of the game.

"We have invested $1bn in 10 years in Africa," Infantino told the assembled delegates in Cape Verde.

At the same event, and for the third time this year, the 54 African nations - carrying more than a quarter of the votes - pledged their unconditional support.

Not only does that buy votes, it buys loyalty too.

And, away from Europe - which has 55 votes - Infantino has that in bucketloads.

Uefa wants a president who is "a respected and unifying figure, deeply rooted in football" with "an unequivocal commitment to development, reform, integrity and independence".

But it has not been able to identify that person itself.

Victor Montagliani, the president of the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football (Concacaf), had been put forward as the most credible opponent. A non-European who could unify opposition to Infantino, and perhaps get others to swap sides.

Yet the Canadian never publicly said he even wanted the job, or to be the face of the campaign against Infantino.

Montagliani has told staff that he intends to stand for re-election with Concacaf, ending any suggestion that he could enter the race at the last moment.

While Infantino's opponents try to find a candidate, Infantino has effectively been out on the campaign trail, clasping hands, taking up photo opportunities.

Only Ramon Vega, the former Tottenham and Switzerland defender, has put himself forward to stand.

But, as was the case four years ago, it seems unlikely Vega will even get the required five letters from the 211 member associations to back his candidacy.

To those on the outside looking in, it might seem preposterous that Infantino will be free to continue, considering the scandal and the reputational damage Fifa has faced.

Such is the power of the position, replacing the president is incredibly difficult.

Fifa has only had five presidents in the past 65 years. And only once, England's Sir Stanley Rous in 1974, has an incumbent lost an election.

When Sepp Blatter resigned in 2015, he did so just eight days after winning re-election.

Uefa still hopes to find a smoking gun through the courts

Next Thursday, Infantino will come face-to-face with his fiercest critics for the first time at a meeting of the Fifa Council in Zurich.

Not just over FFE. But the Fifa Peace Prize, awarded to Donald Trump, and the US President's subsequent intervention in Folarin Balogun's red card at the World Cup.

Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin is expected to attend in person, along with the other eight European representatives - including Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt.

Ceferin, who on Wednesday confirmed he will stand for a fourth term in the role, has been unrelenting in his campaign to replace Infantino.

Even so, BBC Sport understands that internally Uefa accepted some time ago that there was little chance of removing Infantino democratically.

Uefa always had one key hand to play, one tool to deliver a fatal blow - a threat to boycott Fifa's competitions. And it had to be used to get FFE scrapped.

Can it now find a way to get Infantino to stand down, and bow out gracefully?

That would require clear evidence that Infantino had acted against the interests of Fifa and football.

Hours after peace appeared to break out, after Uefa rescinded its boycott threat, it lodged claims in three US courts in an attempt to procure documents related to FFE.

If those papers include anything incriminating, Uefa intends to pursue "criminal mismanagement" through the Swiss courts with the hope of forcing Infantino out.

Up until now there has only been a tit-for-tat legal exchanges.

Even if Infantino does not have an opponent at the ballot box, the battle looks set to continue among the lawyers well into next year.

Politicians, private jets and power - the life of a Fifa president

The map showing world's division over Infantino

Uefa preparing criminal legal action against Infantino

Infantino's initial statements after the fall of FFE included some criticism of those who opposed it.

More recently, he has appeared to be more conciliatory, perhaps aware that this approach may be more effective in winning the war.

"When you go through a journey, sometimes concerns are raised," he told the conference in Cape Verde.

"When they are raised, we have to address them. As far as we are concerned at Fifa, we address them always with the spirit of dialogue and with open arms, an open heart and an open mind. We can always be better and do better."

If, as expected, Infantino does stay then Uefa wants reform of Fifa governance.

But Uefa may come across issues here, too.

Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, the president of the Asian confederation and a Fifa vice-president who sits on the Council, had been a fierce critic of Infantino.

But this week, in a letter sent to Ceferin, Montagliani and Infantino, Al Khalifa distanced himself from a "wholesale redesign of Fifa's governance system".

Al Khalifa said change should be "driven by the football institutions themselves, rather than being outsourced to an external party".

It makes it less likely that, once again, Uefa will get what it wants.

Uefa also wants each country to be paid an additional $10m (£7.6m) from Fifa's vast reserves of around $6bn (£4.5bn).

In a perverse kind of way, Infantino bowing to that demand would probably cement his position even further.

After all, money is a vote-winner for the Fifa president.

articles.title: Manchester City chiefs confident of winning appeal, claim “sporting justice” is on their side
articles.summary: Manchester City have assured their players that they have nothing to fear from the club’s financial case.According to The Sun, the Cityzens insist that “spor...
articles.body:
Manchester City have assured their players that they have nothing to fear from the club's financial case.

According to The Sun , the Cityzens insist that "sporting justice" will prevail as they appeal the Premier League commission's verdict.

City have been found guilty of breaching 114 of the Premier League's financial rules, and rival teams are calling for them to face a historic punishment to match the severity of the situation

The Cityzens remain defiant and have repeatedly denied any wrongdoing. They're also determined to overturn the decision, claiming that the commission's findings contain serious errors.

The club has also accused the Premier League of relying on conspiracy theories and insists that their evidence will prove their innocence.

Gianluigi Donnarumma's agent, Enzo Railo, has said the goalkeeper and his teammates have received reassurances from the club and are not letting the situation affect their preparations.

"Will the Manchester City chaos change anything?" he said. "No, nothing will change for us or for Gigio.

"News comes out periodically. The club has spoken with Gigio, and everyone is calm. Now there are important games against Liverpool and PSG, then sporting justice will take its course.

"But Gigio has had reassurances from Manchester City."

City have formally lodged their appeal and released a statement arguing that the verdict contained material errors of law, principle and fact, making it unsafe.

"The club's firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors of law, principle and fact and is unsafe," their statement read.

"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.

"We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete."

articles.title: 5 questions coach Emma Hayes and the USWNT need to answer before World Cup qualifying
articles.summary: Five questions the United States women's national soccer team needs to answer during this window against Spain before turning its attention to qualifying.
articles.body:
​The United States women's national soccer team kicks off a two-game set this weekend against top-ranked Spain, aiming to solidify its roster plans before the stakes change in November.

​Saturday's match in Washington D.C. and Tuesday's in Chester, Pa., are the Americans' final games before the Concacaf W Championship. The USWNT opens that tournament against El Salvador on Nov. 27, and a win could secure a spot in the 2027 World Cup.

​Facing the world's No. 1 team gives coach Emma Hayes a demanding final rehearsal. Injuries to Naomi Girma and Sam Coffey also give other players another chance to make their case as Hayes evaluates who she can trust if key players remain unavailable.

​Here are five questions the USWNT needs to answer during this window before turning its attention to qualifying.​

What is the midfield plan if Sam Coffey cannot play?

​Coffey's injury affects more than this two-game set against Spain, especially since the midfielder - injured in training with her club, Manchester City - has no return timeline. Hayes must devise an alternative plan for November if Coffey remains out.

​Claire Hutton, the Bay FC midfielder from Bethlehem High, is among the young players ready to take on greater responsibility. Jaelin Howell has joined the roster as Coffey's replacement, while Lindsey Heaps, Rose Lavelle and Lily Yohannes offer more experienced midfield options.

​Hayes needs to decide which group can best protect the defense, move the ball under pressure and connect with the attack. Spain will test all those responsibilities.

​By the end of this two-game window, the USWNT should have a better answer about who anchors the midfield without Coffey and which partnerships work best around them.​

Which defenders can Hayes rely on without Naomi Girma and Emily Sonnett?

​With Girma's recurring injuries and Emily Sonnett's absence, Hayes needs to lock down her defense before qualifying.

​Tierna Davidson, Tara Rudd and Kennedy Wesley are solid options, and first-time call-up Kate Del Fava adds depth. But choosing a replacement is only part of the task. Hayes also needs a back line that communicates well, covers for each other and helps the team play out of its own end.

​Spain can expose gaps and punish defenders who hesitate to step up or track runners.

​These two games will give Hayes time to assess which players form the best defensive unit. If Girma is unavailable in November, Hayes needs an established alternative instead of another search for the right combination.

​Claudia Dickey and Phallon Tullis-Joyce enter camp with 11 and seven senior appearances, respectively. Jordan Silkowitz has yet to make her international debut.

​This window gives Hayes another chance to determine which of the three she trusts for qualifying. Two games against Spain should test which goalkeeper is better at organizing the defense in Girma's absence, how they handle crosses and whether they can choose the right pass when the opposition presses. Who can stay composed under sustained pressure?

​Two matches may not settle the decision, but can give Hayes a clearer idea of which goalkeeper can handle the responsibilities before the qualifying opener.

​What is Hayes' strongest starting attack?

​While Trinity Rodman, Sophia Wilson and Alyssa Thompson give Hayes established offensive options, the question is which attacking combination offers the best chance to score in qualifying.

The question extends beyond choosing three forwards. Hayes needs to see how the front line's movement connects with the midfield, which players stretch the field and who gets into the penalty area to finish chances.

Spain will test whether that group can create chances under pressure and stay connected when the USWNT has less possession.

Before qualifying, Hayes needs a starting attack with clear roles and a dependable way to create chances.

​Ashley Sanchez and Pietra Tordin arrived at fall camp off club production that makes them intriguing options if the USWNT needs a goal.

Sanchez has scored 20 goals for the North Carolina Courage this NWSL season, leading the league's Golden Boot race and tying its single-season scoring record. Tordin has eight goals and nine assists for the Portland Thorns.

Those numbers strengthen their case for a role, but Hayes has said newcomers and players returning after long absences need time to learn the team's tactics and are not expected to start against Spain.

​That makes training and any substitute appearances especially important.

Can Sanchez or Tordin provide a spark off the bench? Can another player provide a different attacking option without disrupting the team's organization?

​Hayes needs to know who she can turn to when the starting attack stalls and what each substitute brings.

articles.title: La idea de Etxeberria es innegociable
articles.standfirst: El nuevo técnico del Alba quiere que todos sepan "qué tipo de equipo vamos a ser" antes de su estreno el lunes en Valladolid
articles.summary: El nuevo técnico del Alba quiere que todos sepan "qué tipo de equipo vamos a ser" antes de su estreno el lunes en Valladolid
articles.body: Joseba Etxeberria ya tiene una idea de su primer once liguero en el Albacete, pero no la desveló. Lo que sí dejó claro es aquello que no está en discusión. Preguntado por si es pronto para ver su impronta en el equipo, el nuevo técnico del Alba separó las alineaciones de la forma de jugar: "Tengo una idea del posible once, pero todavía quedan tres sesiones, queremos todavía tener más información, pero más allá de los que inicien, lo que tengo claro es cómo vamos a jugar y eso va a ser innegociable, ellos lo saben y estamos trabajando cada día en diferentes fases". Esa idea se trabaja por bloques y con un orden: "Hoy toca nuestra fase ofensiva y mañana tocará la fase defensiva, que creo que todo es importante, no es que tengamos un único problema, sino que creo que hay que tocar todas las fases y, sobre todo, que ellos (los jugadores) tengan muy claro de cuál es nuestro modelo, de cuál es nuestra idea". El mensaje no va dirigido sólo al vestuario. Etxeberria quiere que el plan se reconozca también desde la grada: "Lo que quiero es que ellos tengan muy claro qué tipo de equipo vamos a ser y, después, cuando nuestros aficionados nos vean, se den cuenta de hacia dónde va a ir este equipo". El técnico de Elgoibar mantiene el diagnóstico que ya expuso en su presentación: "El equipo tiene argumentos de juego, pero donde tenemos que mejorar es en las áreas, tanto en la eficacia ofensiva como la contundencia defensiva, al final la Segunda División es una categoría muy exigente y esos pequeños detalles ya no son tan pequeños". Sobre el gol confía en los suyos: "tenemos delanteros con gol, que lo han demostrado cada año y esta temporada no va a ser diferente". En la portería no abre debate: "tenemos dos muy buenos porteros y es una demarcación que no me va a quitar sueño". Con la mirada puesta en Valladolid, Etxeberria cree que el Alba tiene opciones de hacer daño: "creo que nosotros podemos hacerles daño, creo que nos podemos adaptar muy bien a su forma de jugar". Sabe que su equipo llega en una situación complicada: "estamos los últimos, pero tenemos tiempo, tenemos argumentos, tenemos herramientas para revertir la situación", y ve a un grupo "herido en ese amor propio, porque son conscientes de que son mejores de lo que dice la clasificación". El partido en Pucela del lunes lo afronta como "una buena oportunidad para lograr la primera victoria" y con un mensaje que ya repitió en su presentación: "creo que es momento de hacer más que de hablar".

articles.title: Manchester United vs Tottenham: Premier League – teams, prediction, lineups
articles.summary: Man United and Tottenham Hotspur managers under increasing pressure ahead of Premier League clash at Old Trafford.
articles.body:
Who: Manchester United vs Tottenham Hotspur What: English Premier League Matchweek 6 Where: Old Trafford, Manchester, United Kingdom When: Saturday, October 9, at 5:30pm (16:30 GMT) How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 13:30 GMT.

Manchester United and Tottenham are accustomed to battling it out at the top end of the Premier League, albeit for UEFA Champions League rankings as opposed the domestic crown in recent years for the former in particular.

Recent seasons have seen both slide to dramatic lows by their standards and a concerned Old Trafford welcomes a Spurs side, whose immediate concerns are far greater than those of the hosts.

Roberto De Zerbi’s struggling North Londoners are bottom of the table with only two points to their name after five games. United’s have one only once in that time and a Spurs win will see the sides level on points.

Al Jazeera Sport takes a closer look at a match that, although early in the season, could well shape the months ahead for both sides and the immediate futures of their managers in a game that has been labelled: “El Sackicko”.

Carrick casts an eye across Manchester to eye City’s woes

United head coach Michael Carrick has plenty of problems of his own, but has called for a swift resolution to Manchester City’s financial charges ⁠case, saying the ⁠long-running process had raised many questions and affected him personally.

Last month, an independent commission found City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over nine ⁠seasons, between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 campaigns, as well as three of four charges concerning their failure to cooperate with the investigation.

City, who currently top the Premier league table as the only side with a perfect record after ⁠five matches, have denied wrongdoing and lodged an appeal.

Carrick spent 12 years at United from 2006 to 2018, winning five Premier League titles and the Champions League among numerous honours, before taking charge in January following Ruben Amorim’s departure.

During his playing career, the 45-year-old former midfielder lost out in two title races won by City, including the 2011-12 campaign when United ‌fell short on goal difference after Sergio Aguero’s dramatic title-clinching goal on the final day.

“It’s thrown up a lot of questions. As it’s still ongoing, and we don’t know how long it’s going to go,” Carrick told a press conference when asked about the City charges.

“It’s affected me personally in different ways over a period of time.”

Would medals make up for lost titles for Man United?

Asked if he wants the titles United missed out on, Carrick said he would reserve judgement until the process was complete.

“I think regardless of anything, a ⁠medal anyway, in any sport in history, I think later on you get the medal and it’s proven at different times,” the Englishman added.

“It’s the moment that you ⁠strive for to win and achieve in that moment, so the medal ⁠here or there, not getting blase about it, but that doesn’t bring the feeling of when you initially win or you don’t win. That’s essentially what we’re all in it for.”

De Zerbi calls on struggling Spurs to react in Man Utd clash

Roberto De Zerbi has urged bottom-of-the-table Tottenham to “react” to the pressure of their crunch clash with fellow strugglers United.

Spurs have been waiting for the chance to erase the bitter taste of a 3-2 home defeat against Aston Villa in their last match before the international break.

And, with scrutiny mounting on the Italian, the Spurs manager demanded his players rise to the challenge against United.

“I’ve been waiting for this game from three weeks. After the defeat at home against Villa, personally I wanted to play the day after,” he told reporters on Friday.

“It was difficult, it was very tough, especially the first week. But it is football. It is part of the situation in this moment. We have to react, to work in this moment.”

Misfiring Tottenham must improve their aim

Tottenham failed to score in their first four league games before finally finding the net twice against Villa.

De Zerbi conceded his team have to improve in attack if they are climb out of the bottom three.

“We created chances to score many other goals in these seven games but we didn’t. We are working to improve in the last third, the assists and the finishing,” he said.

“We are fourth in the table for the team who brings the ball into the opponents’ area the most times.

“It is nothing but it shows we can arrive in the area. We are not good enough to score goals so far when we have clear chances.”

Can Carrick or De Zerbi survive ‘El Sackicko’?

With Carrick also under pressure following their poor start, Tottenham’s trip to Manchester has been dubbed ‘El Sackicko’.

De Zerbi saved Tottenham from relegation after arriving late last season, but that final-day survival feat is unlikely to save him from the axe if results don’t improve soon.

“We are Tottenham. United and Tottenham are still big clubs in the Premier League,” he said.

“We have to deserve to work in this club, playing better and making different results.”

What happened the last time Man United played Tottenham

The sides last met in February in a Premier League encounter at Old Trafford with the home side winning 2-0.

Cristian Romero was shown red on the half-hour mark for Spurs before Bryan Mbeumo and Bruno Fernandes netted the United goals.

When did Tottenham last beat Manchester United?

Spurs famously beat United 1-0 in the UEFA Europa League final in May 2025, thanks to Brennan Johnson’s first-half strike.

The match marked Ange Postecoglou’s last game in charge of the club before being sacked for their lowly league finish.

Ruben Amorim paid the same heavy price the following season.

When did Tottenham last win a match at Manchester United?

Spurs piled the pressure on Amorim early in the 2024-2025 season with a 3-0 Premier League win at Old Trafford.

Johnson gave the away team a third-minute lead, before United had Bruno Fernandes sent off on the stroke of half-time.

Dejan Kulusevski and Dominic Solanke completed the scoring in the second half.

This will be the 205th meeting between the clubs with United winning 96 matches compared to Tottenham’s 56 victories.

Prediction – Manchester United vs Tottenham

The Opta supercomputer has given United a 54 percent chance of winning, while offering Spurs only a 22 percent chance of emerging victorious.

“It’s a bit mixed really through ‌the internationals,” Carrick said. “(Wing back) Patrick Dorgu came off and it looks like he’ll be out probably for a number of weeks.

“(Defender) Noussair Mazraoui came off and took a knock. He’s not quite right yet, we’ll have to ‌see ‌how he is.”

He added that Carlos Baleba was improving, while fellow midfielder Kobbie Mainoo, winger Amad Diallo and forward Marcus Rashford had resumed limited training. Striker Benjamin Sesko remains further away from a return.

Predicted Manchester United starting lineup

Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw; Mainoo, Tielemans; Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford; Cunha

Kulusevski, Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert and Mykhaylo Mudryk all remain sidelined due to injury.

Jan Paul van Hecke has overcome a foot injury, but may miss out after his wife gave birth to twins – the club has said emotional needs will be taken into consideration.

Predicted Tottenham Hotspur starting lineup

Kinsky; Gray, Senesi, Van de Ven, Robertson; Gallagher, Tonali, Fernandes; Savio, Solanke, Marmoush

articles.title: Greek takeaways: What did we learn from England's World Cup play-off win in Crete?
articles.summary: England come away from Greece with a valuable first-leg lead in their Women's World Cup qualifying play-off - but who impressed in the 3-1 victory?
articles.body:
England came away from Greece with a valuable first-leg lead in their Women's World Cup qualifying play-off - but what did we learn?

Sarina Wiegman's side are looking to secure their place in Brazil next year but have to navigate the play-offs after finishing runners-up in their qualification group.

The back-to-back European champions won 3-1 in Crete on Friday night and will need to finish the job against Greece on Tuesday in Leicester (19:30 BST).

The winner of the tie faces Ukraine or Slovakia in round two to decide who will head to Brazil.

Lucy Bronze withdrew from the squad with a minor injury earlier this week, handing a rare opportunity to Manchester United captain Maya le Tissier.

The defender is a key player for her club but struggles to break into the England team with Bronze understandably a tough figure to displace.

Wiegman sees Le Tissier as a right-back as opposed to a centre-back - which is her position at United - and that meant she was handed a start against Greece.

Making her 15th cap, Le Tissier was a standout performer and was rewarded with her first international goal in the 63rd minute, providing optimism for a future without 34-year-old Bronze.

"As soon as we were in possession, she was higher on the pitch and she already came close to a couple of moments with crosses," said Wiegman.

"I'm very happy for her and for the whole team because that was an important goal."

It was just England's third win in their past eight competitive away games.

A 3-1 victory is a pleasing result, but given the gulf in class, Wiegman admitted frustrations at not keeping a clean sheet.

There were familiar lapses in concentration defensively that gave Greece opportunities to pounce. Ioanna Papatheodorou struck the crossbar in the first half, before teeing up Kallisti Brouksair for their goal later on.

Those chances came from England errors and the lack of clean sheet means the door remains open for Greece in the second leg.

"That's up to us. We have to show up on Tuesday, play a good game and then we should be better than Greece," said Wiegman.

"Of course we want to take some more distance [in the scoreline], that's absolutely true, but at the same time we won and that's the most important thing.

"Sometimes we played really well and sometimes we were a bit sloppy. We were a bit frustrated as we wanted to do that better.

"We want to show more than winning, we want to play really well too."

With victory secure, Wiegman was able to hand a debut to 18-year-old Erica Meg Parkinson, as well as Liverpool captain Grace Fisk.

Fisk, 28, had waited more than six years for her debut, having received her first England call-up in 2020 but Parkinson has broken through at pace this season.

The teenager was unexpectedly named in Wiegman's squad in March, having only made the jump up to England's Under-23s a few months earlier.

She secured a move to the United States this summer, joining North Carolina Courage from Portuguese side Valadares Gaia, and came on in the 85th minute.

This week defender Esme Morgan said: "She's a really intelligent player. She has incredibly good movement and timing, picking up pockets for players to find her.

"She's really comfortable receiving [the ball] in tight spaces, she's strong holding off players, very aggressive in her tackling and wins back a lot of balls.

"I've been really impressed with Erica since she came into camp and also from playing against her in the National Women's Soccer League."

Why England teenager Parkinson has a mindset coach

Parkinson's debut added to the debate of who Wiegman's preferred number 10 is.

She is one of many options available, including Chelsea forward Lauren James, who was given a creative, free role against Greece.

James showed flashes of quality and nonchalantly lobbed goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti from 30 yards in the first half, but her effort was ruled out for offside.

Other options include Manchester City's Grace Clinton and Manchester United's Ella Toone, who were both recalled to the squad to cover injuries with Aston Villa's Lucia Kendall among those to drop out.

Laura Blindkilde Brown started in that position with James in Crete, while Beth Mead and Jess Park have also played there before.

The position was a difficult one for Wiegman to nail down at Euro 2025 and more than a year later, the question of who is England's best number 10 remains.

"I see there is a lot of competition in that position, where we have a lot of options with different players, who have different qualities," said Wiegman.

"You can call it a question mark but I call it many options. Today we had two 10s and sometimes three. [James] was one of them."

Local media had questioned why the game wasn't being played in Greece's capital city Athens.

And there was an eerie atmosphere with fewer than 4,000 fans in the 26,000-capacity stadium in Heraklion, Crete.

The Lionesses are also not used to being in play-offs, a route they are having to take after finishing runners-up to world champions Spain in their qualifying group.

But Georgia Stanway, this year's top scorer for England, once again turned up when they needed her to and she opened the scoring after a neat, incisive passing move, in a frustrating first half.

That was the spark England needed as they lacked ruthlessness and failed to capitalise on their dominance - an aspect of their game that needs improving.

"I think we made it a bit harder. Greece were well prepared and disciplined. We struggled when they tried to press us," added Wiegman.

"We could have scored more than the three goals. There are lots of things to take. I have seen some fluid moments but I want more.

"The final ball, final cross and the positions can be better. Of course, we are working on that. We have an opportunity to improve that on Tuesday."

articles.title: West Ham 1-1 QPR: Jarrod Bowen's stoppage-time penalty saved by Pierce Charles as Hammers held at home on return from international break
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between West Ham United and Queens Park Rangers at the London Stadium on Friday night; Jarrod Bowen's 91st-minute penalty saved by Pierce Charles as points shared on return from extended international break
articles.body:
Nicolas Madsen put Rangers 1-0 up, rolling home a penalty awarded in highly controversial circumstances.

But the Hammers came alive as the conclusion approached, with Bowen slamming in his seventh goal of the season to equalise after his first shot was blocked.

In the 90th minute, Amadou Mbengue tugged the shirt of Pablo in the penalty area and Bowen had the chance to win it from the spot.

But Pierce Charles dived low to his left to keep out the initial effort, then reacted in a flash to tip Arne Engels' follow-up over the bar.

How a dramatic evening unfolded in East London

Nuno Espirito Santo's side thumped Wrexham 6-0 in their last home game , but found themselves nowhere near that level in the first half. The display was sedate - they had two shots, with a total xG value of 0.07 - and they found themselves behind after only 18 minutes.

Tomas Soucek - making his first appearance of the season after recovering from an ankle injury sustained at the World Cup - slid in on Paul Smyth as the QPR livewire looked to break into the box.

The Czech midfielder got the ball - but referee Ruebyn Ricardo saw otherwise and pointed to the spot. Soucek's reaction was one of sheer disbelief.

"That's definitely not a penalty. No way on Earth. This is an absolute howler," said Lee Hendrie on co-commentary.

Speaking at half-time, studio guest Rob Green added: "The referee didn't let the situation breathe. He didn't give himself a moment to think: 'hold on a minute, what's actually happened here?'

"He just saw the ball move, the player move, the player fall over and gave the penalty."

Madsen coolly tucked away the penalty - and until the 70th minute that was all that separated the sides.

But West Ham came alive and were level when Bowen darted away from substitute Tariq Lamptey, hit one shot that was blocked, then made no mistake with the second.

The captain was denied another by a sharp Charles save, but with 90 minutes on the clock, Mbengue's overzealous tug was spotted by the officials and Bowen had the chance to be the hero once again.

Instead it was Charles who took the plaudits with two brilliant quickfire saves to preserve the point that sees QPR climb to fifth.

Soucek: Ref has admitted he was wrong - but he didn't speak to me on the pitch

West Ham 's Tomas Soucek speaking to Sky Sports:

"I was so happy I won the challenge and recovered the ball!

"Straight away, I didn't know what the referee was doing and, from my perspective, it's a massive, massive mistake.

"We are just disappointed because, when I saw it inside, it looks even worse. I can't change it, but I cannot accept it.

"After the game, he told me he was wrong, but during the game, he just didn't want to speak with me any more.

"I was disappointed he didn't even want to speak with me so he could explain to me what he saw.

"I am disappointed because it had a big impact on me, but even more on the team. It was tough to take, but at least we got a point."

Nuno: We have the quality to do much better

West Ham 's Nuno Espirito Santo speaking to Sky Sports:

"We could have won in the end, but we didn't start the game well. Once again, we were not precise in our passing, the game didn't flow. The first half was not good.

"We were able to react from a goal down and we had chances to win the game until the end.

"We always know, after an international break, there's a question mark over the players, also the players that have been involved in national teams. It was maybe an explanation, but we expect much more. We have enough quality to do much better."

On the controversial penalty award: "Unfortunately, it's not a good decision. The ref didn't get it right in that moment. The images are clear. There's not much more to say about that."

articles.title: Barça - Getafe: Los culés, a un paso de la historia
articles.standfirst: Confían en seguir con su exitosa trayectoria de antes del parón por las selecciones
articles.summary: Confían en seguir con su exitosa trayectoria de antes del parón por las selecciones
articles.body: EEl Barcelona retoma esta tarde la competición con el deseo y la intención de mantener el excelente nivel mostrado hasta el parón de selecciones: ganó con autoridad y supremacía los siete primeros partidos de LaLiga. Líder en solitario de la clasificación, el Barça intentará sumar su octavo éxito consecutivo y el 23 como local contra un Getafe irregular que ocupa la mitad de la tabla. El bloque de Hansi Flick vuelve hoy a la competición y lo hace con la voluntad de ampliar, tras su cruce con el equipo madrileño, su exitosa trayectoria de este curso y de hacer historia. Sólo hay un equipo culé que haya ganado los ocho primeros encuentros: fue el Barça del Tata Martino de la temporada 13-14. El reto es importante, pero las estadísticas favorecen a los azulgranas en sus cruces contra el Getafe. En los 21 partidos que han jugado entre LaLiga y la Copa del Rey contra el conjunto azulón en el Spotify Camp Nou, los azulgranas se han impuesto en 17 ocasiones y han empatado en 4. No conocen, por lo tanto, la derrota. Pero sumar la octava victoria consecutiva en este arranque no es la única gesta que ambicionan conquistar esta jornada. Los culés están ante otra gran hazaña. El Barça se impuso (6-0) el 14 de septiembre de 2025 al Valencia en la cuarta jornada de la competición doméstica de la campaña 25-26 en el Estadi Johan Cruyff, y desde entonces los de Hansi Flick han ganado los 22 compromisos ligueros que han disputado como locales. Están a tres triunfos de igualar la mejor racha de su historia, lograda entre la jornada 22 de la Liga 1951-52 y la 12 de la 1953-54, con 25 victorias de forma consecutiva en casa. Para equipararle, deberán superar a Getafe, Real Madrid y Alavés. Para lograr estas hazañas, el técnico germano debe gestionar los minutos de sus hombres: ha tenido a 17 futbolistas repartidos con sus respectivas selecciones. El preparador germano dosificará a algunos de sus jugadores, porque, además, el calendario inmediato no da tregua a los catalanes. El próximo martes se miden al Galatasaray en Turquía, y en dos semanas, afrontan cinco encuentros. Por ello, Flick no forzará el regreso de Raphinha, que será baja seguro en los dos próximos compromisos por sus molestias en la parte posterior del muslo derecho. El técnico confirmó que Gabriel Jesus ocupará esta tarde su posición en la delantera. También reveló que Joan García está recuperado de su dolencia en la rodilla derecha y saldrá de inicio bajo palos en el cruce en el Spotify Camp Nou. El Getafe, por su parte, arrancará un particular Tourmalet que llevará a los de Bordalás a jugar hasta nueve compromisos en apenas un mes. El conjunto azulón aterriza esta tarde en el feudo azulgrana consciente del gran momento del rival, pero buscando un triunfo que sería histórico. Los del sur de Madrid aún no han ganado en territorio barcelonés y, tres puntos serían vitales para afrontar con garantías este inicio de montaña ruda al que se enfrentará el cuadro getafense y coger la máxima moral. El conjunto madrileño llega con las ya conocidas bajas por lesión de Christantus Uche y Juanmi y con la duda de Satriano, que tuvo que abandonar la concentración con Uruguay en este pasado parón por una inflamación de rodilla. Bordalás señaló que confía en que el internacional charrúa llegue, aunque no aseguró si su presencia sería finalmente una realidad.

articles.title: Funes: "En la segunda parte solo ha habido un equipo"
articles.standfirst: El técnico valora positivamente el punto pese a que el Málaga no gana
articles.summary: El técnico valora positivamente el punto pese a que el Málaga no gana
articles.body: El Málaga rescató un punto ante el Espanyol en La Rosaleda gracias al gol de Adrián Niño en el tramo final. Un empate que dejó un sabor agridulce a Juanfran Funes, satisfecho con la reacción de su equipo tras el descanso, pero consciente de que mereció más. "Hemos sido capaces de ir a por el partido en la segunda parte. Solo ha habido un equipo", aseguró el técnico malaguista, que destacó la superioridad de los suyos tras el descanso. El entrenador reconoció que el equipo debe mejorar su contundencia en el área rival, aunque se mostró convencido de que los goles llegarán si mantienen ese nivel de juego. Funes también valoró los debuts de Fernando Calero y Adam Aznou, que todavía necesitan ritmo de competición. "No estaban preparados para afrontar un encuentro completo, pero nos han dado soluciones. Ha sido impresionante el esfuerzo de los chavales", explicó. El entrenador no descartó la posibilidad de jugar con dos delanteros desde el inicio en próximos partidos. "Este año va a haber partidos en los que empezaremos con dos delanteros", avanzó, dejando abierta esa alternativa para dar más recursos al ataque blanquiazul. Sobre el posible penalti no señalado a Chupete, Funes reconoció que desde el banquillo lo vieron claro, aunque evitó responsabilizar al arbitraje del resultado. "El árbitro no ha sido decisivo en lo que ha ocurrido", afirmó. Por último, el técnico destacó el apoyo de La Rosaleda y confió en que el empate ayude a cambiar la dinámica del equipo. "Pueden ser partidos que cambien inercias. Nos va a dar un empujón muy fuerte", aseguró, antes de insistir en que el Málaga no se sintió inferior al Espanyol y que la segunda mitad refuerza la confianza del grupo.

articles.title: Gritos de "Bryan, muérete" en La Rosaleda y el jugador se defiende
articles.standfirst: El delantero del Espanyol asegura que no mandó ningún mensaje a la afición tras su gol
articles.summary: El delantero del Espanyol asegura que no mandó ningún mensaje a la afición tras su gol
articles.body: Bryan Zaragoza fue el protagonista positivo para el Espanyol y el negativo para el Málaga en el regreso de LaLiga a La Rosaleda. El atacante malagueño sacó lo peor del estadio de Martiricos con la celebración de su gol, un tanto de bella factura que puso por delante al conjunto perico en la primera mitad y que estuvo cerca de darle los tres puntos al equipo catalán. El extremo recibió en la banda, encaró a Puga y Calero, se deshizo de ambos con una gran acción individual y batió a Herrero para firmar el 0-1. Pero lo que más encendió a La Rosaleda llegó después. Bryan se llevó la mano a la oreja en dirección a la grada y provocó a la afición malaguista durante su celebración. La historia viene de lejos. Bryan Zaragoza nunca llegó a entrar en la cantera del Málaga CF cuando se encontraba en edad juvenil. Después de pasar por el CD Tiro Pichón y el CD Conejito de Málaga, el futbolista realizó las pruebas para incorporarse a La Academia blanquiazul, pero los responsables de la cantera no apostaron por él. Tampoco lo hicieron el Betis o el Valladolid, club con el que también llegó a realizar una prueba. Finalmente fue el Granada el que confió en aquel menudo atacante que acabaría llegando a la élite. El partido tuvo más capítulos de tensión. Bryan protagonizó un encontronazo con Carlos Puga, después de que ambos chocaran sus cabezas en una acción que terminó con un conato de bronca. El colegiado resolvió la situación mostrando amarilla a los dos futbolistas. En ese momento, parte de La Rosaleda respondió con un cántico absolutamente fuera de lugar: “Bryan, muérete”. Una expresión que no representa al aficionado malaguista y que sobró por completo en un partido que ya estaba cargado de tensión. Bryan, lejos de rebajar el ambiente, continuó haciendo gestos hacia la grada y cada balón que tocó estuvo acompañado de una sonora pitada. La Rosaleda convirtió cada intervención del malagueño en un pequeño pulso entre jugador y afición. El extremo acabó siendo sustituido en el minuto 73 y volvió a marcharse entre los abucheos de la grada. El jugador no daba crédito a lo que le había sucedido y a la conclusión del partido habló sobre lo que le tocó vivir sobre el terreno de juego. ¿Celebración con mensaje? No había mensaje a la grada. Yo al Málaga le tengo cariño y le tengo respeto, pero nunca he jugado aquí y llevo tiempo que no me encuentro con el gol y si marco, lo voy a celebrar. Todo el mundo me tiene que comprender. Yo no mando ningún mensaje a la afición. Al Málaga lo respeto porque es el club de mi ciudad, pero si marco ¿por qué no lo puedo celebrar? Tampoco entiendo la rabia hacia mí. No he hecho nada malo. Sólo he metido un gol y lo he celebrado. No he hecho ningún gesto a la grada" Nunca jugó en el Málaga. "Podía haber jugado, pero nunca me han querido. Nunca he jugado. Se han equivocado. Me he encontrado con el gol, me sentía feliz y lo he celebrado. Le he dedicado el gol a mi hijo y a mi mujer y sí le ha sentado mal a alguno, pido perdón. No quiero que nadie se sienta ofendido". Sensaciones tras el empate: "Jodidos, muy jodidos. Creo que ellos han jugado bien. El empate es un resultado más o menos justo. En al primera parte tuvimos varias ocasiones para ganar. Nos vamos con muy mal sabor de boca porque el gol ha sido prácticamente en la última jugada". Próximo partidos: "Esto nos tiene que doler a todos. Tenemos que subir el ritmo y espabilar"

articles.title: Lars Ricken and Niko Kovac react to “pure disappointment” for Borussia Dortmund
articles.summary: Borussia Dortmund’s winning streak came to an end on Friday evening as they conceded two late goals against Werder Bremen. Managing director Lars Ricken and...
articles.body:
Borussia Dortmund's winning streak came to an end on Friday evening as they conceded two late goals against Werder Bremen. Managing director Lars Ricken and head coach Niko Kovac admit the disappointment in the manner they threw away a six-game streak in all competitions.

"It's pure disappointment," Ricken said in the mixed zone after the final whistle. "We knew it was going to be a difficult game. Nevertheless, we came in well and had an extremely large amount of possession.

"Bremen then attacked with the courage of despair and did well. In the end, you have to look forward. We have a lot of tasks ahead of us now. As disappointed as we are now, we can also be confident with our start in the league."

"We dominated the opponent for 88 minutes in such a way that we had them in the corner," Kovac reacted as his team started the busy schedule with a poor result. "But we didn't manage to finish the last eight minutes as we should have.

"We have to blame ourselves for that. We had chances in the second half. We are disappointed, of course. We dropped two points. Hopefully, we will learn our lessons from the last eight minutes."

Borussia Dortmund's next game will be against fellow Black and Yellows Bodø/Glimt in the Champions League. They will then travel to struggling Union Berlin in matchday 6 Bundesliga action.

articles.title: Calero: "Habría sido muy duro irse de vacío"
articles.standfirst: El defensa debutó ante su exequipo
articles.summary: El defensa debutó ante su exequipo
articles.body: Fernando Calero debutó como titular con el Málaga CF ante su exequipo, el Espanyol, en un partido que terminó con empate (1-1). El central, que llevaba casi dos meses sin competir, tuvo que abandonar el terreno de juego por calambres después de un estreno en el que mostró buenas maneras con el balón, aunque sufrió en algunas acciones defensivas. El defensa blanquiazul considera que el Málaga hizo méritos para conseguir algo más que el empate. "Después de un partido bastante completo por nuestra parte habría sido muy duro irse de vacío", reconoció tras el encuentro. Calero explicó que el Espanyol hizo daño a la contra durante la primera mitad, pero destacó la reacción malaguista tras el descanso. "En la segunda parte hemos salido con otra mentalidad y hemos volcado el juego hacia el área rival y hemos conseguido el empate", señaló. En el plano personal, el central se mostró satisfecho con su debut, pese a no poder completar los 90 minutos. "Me he sentido muy cómodo y a gusto. Sabía que me iba a costar porque llevaba mucho sin jugar. He intentado dar el máximo de mí", explicó. El defensa también valoró positivamente su entendimiento con Recio en el centro de la zaga. "Muy bien con Recio. Recio está increíble. Nos hemos compenetrado muy bien y sabíamos que teníamos que estar cerca de Roberto", comentó. Por último, Calero transmitió confianza en la capacidad ofensiva del equipo y descartó que exista nerviosismo por la falta de gol. "Tenemos grandísimos finalizadores y jugadores que tienen mucho talento ofensivo. No estoy nervioso y acabarán llegando los goles", concluyó.

articles.title: Man City charges: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta says he has clear conscience over his time at Etihad after serious breaches of financial rules
articles.summary: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta was asked about Manchester City being found to have arranged "sham contracts" with commercial partners to inflate revenues during a period in which he worked as Pep Guardiola's assistant; City have lodged an appeal and deny the chargers
articles.body:
The investigation covered two years in which Arteta was working as assistant to manager Pep Guardiola but, in an otherwise guarded press conference, the Arsenal boss answered "yes" when asked if he had a clear conscience.

Arteta, who this week signed a new four-year contract as Arsenal manager , faced a string of questions over the City verdict by journalists but repeatedly insisted he would not comment further until the outcome of City's appeal is known.

"The thing is that this has been going for various years," he said.

"The process is still not finished, so it's very difficult to express how I feel because it's not resolved. When it's resolved, I can talk with clarity and tell you exactly how I feel.

"I think that process has to be resolved in a way. And we need to trust that the people who are in charge doing that will do it in the timeframe that they believe is best for everybody."

Arteta spent three-and-a-half seasons working with Guardiola, including the 2016/17 and 2017/18 campaigns, when City won back-to-back Premier League titles, an FA Cup and two League Cups, before leaving the club to take charge of Arsenal in 2019.

According to the independent commission, City artificially inflated their sponsorship income by £264.3m across the 2016/17 and 2017/18 seasons, a period during which their signings included John Stones, Aymeric Laporte, Bernardo Silva, Ederson and Kyle Walker.

Arteta refused to comment when asked if his memories of working at City had been tainted.

When asked whether he was pleased to have won the Premier League title for Arsenal before the verdict, he said: "I feel proud and very emotional when I think about how we won it, the moments that we had together. It's a unique and genuine feeling that I have."

Arteta: Premier League still best in the world

Arteta insisted the Premier League will "100 per cent" continue to be the best league in the world despite questions of integrity being thrown up by the City verdict.

"It's the best league in the world for many reasons," he added.

"I've been here for over 20 years and it will continue to be the best league in the world. I feel privileged to be where I am.

"And there are a few clubs who have been extremely good and managed resources in an intelligent way. And we suffered from that a few weeks ago [with their defeat to Brighton]."

However, following comments by Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner, who said the Premier League has been "damaged" by City being found guilty, Arteta admitted he was unsure about the impact on the competition's reputation globally.

"I want to think that it doesn't [damage the Premier League] but I don't know," he said. "And certainly it's not in our control.

"In our control is to bring everything we can individually to the club, to maintain the position we have to be the best league in the world."
